Where is the Hardin County Clerk, and what does the office hold for a home seller?

The clerk works from Suite 103 of the Hardin County Government Building, 150 N. Provident Way, Elizabethtown, KY 42701, and answers at 270-765-2171. Doors are open weekdays from 7:45 in the morning until 4:30 in the afternoon. A branch at 101 W. Lincoln Trail Blvd in Radcliff takes vehicle registrations Tuesday through Thursday from 8 to 4, but deeds go to Elizabethtown.

This is the county's keeper of deeds, mortgages, wills, plats, liens, assumed names and marriage records, and it also issues vehicle titles and tags and runs elections. A seller meets the office three ways: when the deed to the buyer is recorded, when an old mortgage needs a release of record, and when a bill that missed the sheriff's April 15 cutoff has moved to the clerk.

Courthouse fires in 1864 and 1932 destroyed county records, so a title examiner working on a very old chain may find gaps that predate the present 1934 courthouse.

Can I search Hardin County land records online?

Yes. The clerk's website runs an eSearch name search that works as a guest, and it indexes far more than deeds. The index types include deeds, mortgages, deeds of release, affidavits of descent, plats, powers of attorney, restrictions, wills, lis pendens, mechanics liens and ad valorem liens, along with fiscal court minutes and ordinances.

For a seller, two searches pay off before listing. A search on your own name should show the mortgage and, once paid, a deed of release. A search for liens should show nothing left unreleased, since a lien filed against a prior owner or a contractor can surface at a title company in the final week.

What does Kentucky require in a deed the Hardin County Clerk will accept?

The clerk records deeds for property in Hardin County, and it must turn away a deed that breaks a content rule in KRS 382.135 or KRS 382.110. Title attorneys cover these items routinely. A family transfer written from a form is where gaps show up.

  • Full names and mailing addresses for both parties.
  • The full price, backed by a notarized certificate signed by both sides. A gift deed carries a certificate saying so, with an estimated fair cash value.
  • An in care of address for the bill of the year of transfer.
  • The source of the grantor's title, by deed book and page when it came from a recorded deed, or a plain explanation when it came by inheritance.

An estate that passes land by will or intestacy adds one more filing: the personal representative lodges an affidavit listing who received each parcel and what it was valued at.

Which recording charges does the Hardin County Clerk list?

The clerk posts a fee schedule alongside its formatting rules. Paper should be white and unbound, black ink, no seals or highlighter, with a three inch blank strip across the top of page one. Electronic filers use Simplifile, ePn or CSC.

Sample Hardin County Clerk recording charges

Mortgage$80.00

Affidavit of descent and distribution$50.00

Will$47.00

Most documents add $3.00 for every page past five and $4.00 per extra reference, and a mortgage adds $3.00 per page past thirty. Confirm the total with the clerk before mailing a packet.

How much transfer tax does the seller owe at the Hardin County Clerk?

The grantor pays fifty cents per $500 block of value, with any leftover amount counted as a full block, under KRS 142.050. The clerk computes it from the value stated in the deed, collects before accepting the paper, and certifies the payment date and amount on the deed itself. The tax is collected once per transaction, in whichever county the deed is filed. The clerk keeps 5 percent for the work, and the rest goes to the county treasurer every three months for the general fund. On a $300,000 sale that is 600 blocks, or $300. On a house priced at the Census median value of $225,800 it is 452 blocks, or $226.

Foreclosure deeds, deeds in lieu, transfers between spouses in a divorce, partitions, and parent to child gifts with only nominal consideration are among the exemptions. When a deed carries no stated price, the tax is figured on the open market estimate.

What happens when the clerk rejects a deed or a deed arrives late?

The statute bars the clerk from lodging a deed that fails the content rules, so a rejected package usually means a corrected deed, a new notarization and a second trip. A deed recorded in error still counts as notice to later buyers and creditors, but the defect can still draw questions from a title insurer.

Timing rules apply to some transfers. A lender that takes a deed in lieu of foreclosure must file it with the clerk within 45 days of signing. A grantee under a deed from a court appointed commissioner has five business days from receipt to file. If you are the seller on either kind of transfer, confirm with the other side that the deed has been filed before you consider the matter closed.

Which other recordings might a Hardin County seller need?

Selling often trips over small filings. These come up most often, with the clerk's charges.

  • Release of a paid mortgage: $46.00.
  • Affidavit of descent and distribution after an inheritance: $50.00.
  • Power of attorney: $50.00, and a revocation: $46.00.
  • Release of a mechanics lien: $46.00, or $60.00 for a bond that releases it.
  • Release of a judgment lien or federal tax lien: $46.00. A state tax lien release costs $5.00.
  • City lien and city release: $23.00.
  • Notary service at the counter: $5.00 per acknowledgement plus $2.00 per notarization.

None of these replaces a title search, but ordering them early prevents the delay of a lender waiting on a release.

Where does the clerk fit into unpaid property tax in Hardin County?

The sheriff's page sends sellers to the clerk for payoff on any delinquent bill from a prior year. After April 15 a bill is a certificate of delinquency in the clerk's office, and the clerk's page offers a delinquent tax calculator and tax sale information. The recording schedule also lists $30.00 to record a certificate assignment and $46.00 for a reassignment or release.

Request a payoff in writing, dated near the closing date, because interest accrues monthly. If a third party bought the certificate, the payoff goes to that buyer.

What do Census figures say about the people who buy and sell in Hardin County?

The Census Bureau counts 44,622 households with 2.44 people each, and 84.6 percent of residents had not moved in the past year. Median gross rent is $971, per capita income $37,638, and 12,344 residents are veterans.

With Fort Knox in the county, some sellers and buyers work to a fixed report date. A deed that meets every content rule on the first attempt avoids a trip back to Suite 103.

Can a deed be e-recorded in Hardin County, Kentucky?

Yes. The Hardin County Clerk lists Simplifile, ePn and CSC as accepted electronic recording vendors.

How much is a mortgage release at the Hardin County Clerk?

$46.00 for a full or partial release, plus $3.00 for each page past five. The deed itself is $50.00.

How much is transfer tax on a $300,000 Hardin County sale?

$300. The rate is $0.50 per $500 of value, so 600 blocks of $500 times fifty cents, paid by the seller when the deed is filed.

Does the Radcliff branch record deeds?

No. The Radcliff branch at 101 W. Lincoln Trail Blvd handles vehicle registration on Tuesday through Thursday. Deeds are recorded at Suite 103, 150 N. Provident Way, Elizabethtown.

Is a state tax lien release cheaper than a federal one in Hardin County?

Yes. The clerk charges $5.00 to record a state tax lien or its release and $46.00 for a federal tax lien or release.

What can the Warren County Clerk's office do for a home seller?

When a Bowling Green house changes hands, the deed ends up in this office. The clerk lists elections, motor vehicles and public land records as the three main jobs, and adds marriage licenses, notary commissions and delinquent property taxes to the list.

  • Mailing address: P.O. Box 478, Bowling Green, KY 42102.
  • Phone: (270) 842-9416. The fax for legal recordings is (270) 843-5319.
  • Doors open weekdays from 8:00 am until 4:30 pm.
  • The deed room is on the building's bottom floor, with public terminals and a deputy records clerk on hand to get you started.

Some errands belong elsewhere. Driver's licenses come from the state Transportation Cabinet, and traffic citations go to the Circuit Clerk at 1001 Center St., Suite 102.

The clerk's message on the site calls Warren the fastest growing county in Kentucky.

Which county records a Kentucky deed?

The clerk where the land sits, or where most of a split parcel sits. That rule comes from KRS 382.110, which also bars a clerk from taking a deed that skips the seller's source of title. When the seller bought by a recorded deed, the new one cites that earlier deed's book, page and recording date. An heir states how and from whom the property came.

A 2026 act amended the section, effective July 15, 2026. A lender taking a deed in lieu of foreclosure has 45 days to file it.

What must a deed say before Warren County will file it?

The contents come from KRS 382.135, and a deed lacking any item is refused. A deed from a title attorney normally covers all of them.

  • Full names and mailing addresses for the grantor and grantee.
  • The whole consideration paid.
  • A forwarding address for the tax bill of the year of transfer.
  • A sworn, notarized statement signed by both parties that the price on the deed is the whole price. A gift instead needs a statement saying so and estimating fair cash value.

When a house passes through an estate, the personal representative files a separate affidavit in every county with estate land, naming who gets what and its value. The clerk's FAQ adds a warning that staff cannot do a title search or answer whether liens exist, so leave that to a title company.

What are the Warren County recording charges?

A posted fee schedule dated January 1, 2020 sits on the clerk's fees and vendors page. For most documents a charge of $3.00 applies to each page beyond five. Mortgages and releases of mortgage work differently, adding $5.00 for each page beyond thirty.

Copies are cheaper: $.50 a page from a public terminal, $5 for a certified copy of up to three pages with $.50 for each more, and $3 for a big plat. Call before you mail a package to get the exact total.

What transfer tax comes due at the counter?

The grantor pays fifty cents per $500 of value, rounding any remainder up. KRS 142.050 makes the clerk do the math and take payment before accepting the deed. The clerk's cut is 5 percent, and the treasurer gets the remainder every quarter.

Value means the whole price including liens, or the estimated open market price for a gift. Compare two sales:

  • A $258,000 sale divides into 516 blocks, so the tax is exactly $258.00.
  • A $312,400 sale leaves a part block, giving 625 blocks and $312.50.

The statute exempts many ordinary transfers, such as foreclosure deeds, deeds that grant or release security for a debt, divorce transfers between spouses, partitions, tax sales, and nominal price deeds from parent to child or grandparent to grandchild. Match your deed to the statute's wording before counting on an exemption.

How do I look up land records in Warren County?

Two routes exist. You can sit at a terminal in the deed room, or you can use eCCLIX, a subscription service from a records vendor. Personal users get five free searches a day, and commercial users pay a subscription. Because the index follows party names and document types, an address search will not work. Look the owner up on the PVA's site first, then search the clerk's records by name.

Staff will point out how the system works but will not run the search for you. DocAlert is another service the clerk promotes. It is free and emails you when a mortgage or deed is filed under your name, which helps owners of vacant rentals or land spot fraud.

Four vendors accept electronic recordings:

  • Simplifile, (800) 460-5657
  • CSC, (866) 652-0111
  • ePN, (888) 325-3365
  • Hopdox, (385) 501-5103 ext. 010

Where do unpaid property taxes end up in Warren County?

After April 15 the sheriff's open bills belong to the clerk. The office takes payments until its annual sale, runs a current list in PDF, and takes buyer registrations for the sale held at its East 10th Avenue office. Most outside buyers must also register with the state first, so the clerk sends them to the Department of Revenue's form. Call for a payoff before closing, because interest and commissions keep growing each month and the lien can travel with the land for 11 years.

What does a Warren County closing also depend on?

Work done without a permit is where closings tend to snag. Warren County's Division for Building Services at 1141 State Street handles permits outside Bowling Green and Oakland and states that all new construction needs one. Sheds starting at 120 square feet, decks and pools need permits too, and the county's stormwater office generally bars fences, sheds, pools and additions inside a drainage easement without a written exception, and Bowling Green has its own inspector at (270) 393-3615.

Warren County dates to 1796, when it was cut from Logan County. Confederate forces held the area in September 1861 until Union troops took it on February 14, 1862, and the L&N Railroad arrived in 1859. A farm with a long chain of title may have early records in Logan County rather than here, so ask the deed room where to look.

Prices set Warren apart from the two other counties in this guide: Census QuickFacts shows a $258,000 midpoint, against $172,000 in Trimble County and $104,500 in Union County. Renters occupy 44.4 percent of homes, and the median rent is $1,002.

A tenant, a probate delay, half finished repairs or unpaid taxes need not hold up a sale, since a cash buyer will purchase as is.

Frequently asked questions

Where is a deed recorded in Warren County?

At the Warren County Clerk's office, reached by mail at P.O. Box 478, Bowling Green, KY 42102, or by phone at (270) 842-9416. Four e-recording vendors also send documents electronically.

How much does Warren County charge to record a deed?

The base fee is $50, with $3.00 added for each page past the fifth. A deed of correction costs $46. Transfer tax is extra, and the seller covers it.

Can I find a Warren County deed using only the address?

No. The clerk indexes by party names and document types. Find the owner by address on the PVA's website first, then search the clerk's index under that name.

Will clerk staff check my title?

No. Staff can demonstrate the index, yet they are not permitted to run a title search or declare a property free of liens. Hire a title company or attorney for that.

Who owes Kentucky's transfer tax on a house sale?

It falls on the grantor in the deed, at half a dollar per $500 of value. The clerk collects it first, then records the deed.

Where in Barren County is a deed recorded?

The Barren County Clerk's office, in the Barren County Government Center on the north side of the square, at 117 North Public Square, Suite 1A, Glasgow, KY 42141 (phone 270-651-3783), records every deed and mortgage on Barren County land.

Under KRS 382.110 the filing belongs to the county containing the land. A house in Cave City, Park City, Glasgow or near Barren River Lake therefore goes on record in Glasgow, wherever the seller now lives. The same Legal Records Division collects delinquent real estate taxes, so back taxes on a house surface at this counter too.

What should a home seller know about Barren County itself?

The county dates to 1798, spans roughly 500 square miles of south-central Kentucky and is governed from Glasgow, its largest city. Interstate 65 crosses the northwest corner, the Cumberland Expressway serves the county, and US 31E, 31W and 68 pass through it. Part of Mammoth Cave National Park falls inside the line, and visitors keep motels and restaurants busy around Cave City.

  • Estimated 2025 population: 45,641, which is 2.6 percent above the April 2020 base.
  • Half of owner-occupied houses were worth more than $178,000 in the 2020 to 2024 Census survey.
  • Owners live in 65.2 percent of 18,017 households, which leaves roughly a third of occupied homes as rentals.
  • Middle household income: $50,628. Middle gross rent: $796.
  • Housing units: 20,957 as of July 2025.

Three school systems cover the county: Barren County Schools, Glasgow Independent Schools, and Caverna Independent Schools around Cave City, which reaches into Hart County as well. Buyers often ask which of the three serves a particular house.

What else does the Barren County Clerk's office handle?

Besides land records, the Glasgow office issues marriage licenses, notary commissions and going-out-of-business licenses. Its Motor Vehicle Division registers or renews more than 40,000 vehicles a year, collects Barren County vehicle taxes including motorboats, issues decals, plates and disabled parking permits, and files liens on titled collateral. The clerk's page describes the Legal Records Division as the place that records and indexes every real estate document, among them powers of attorney, assignments, releases and UCC fixture filings.

For a home seller the practical lesson is that one trip covers several errands. A closing agent can bring the deed and a release in the same visit.

How much does it cost to record a deed at the Barren County Clerk?

The schedule on the clerk's site took effect January 1, 2020, and the office points to KRS 64.012 and House Bill 537 as its basis. Pages beyond the fifth cost $3 each on most filings, while a mortgage waits until page thirty-one for that surcharge.

Barren County Clerk minimum recording fees, as posted for January 1, 2020 (barren.countyclerk.us)

KRS 142.010 separately imposes a $4 state tax on a real property conveyance, collected by the clerk. Request one all-in figure at the counter.

Why does the Barren County Clerk reject deeds?

The clerk's recording page posts the usual reasons a filing comes back. Nearly all can be prevented, and a returned deed can push a closing back.

  • The document is not notarized, or the notary left off an expiration date or the date of notarization.
  • The filing fee is wrong or the check is unsigned.
  • The title source is incomplete, or there is no legal description of the property.
  • No in-care-of address appears for the tax bill.
  • The grantor or grantee mailing address is missing.
  • A copy was submitted where an original is required.
  • A power of attorney lacks two disinterested witnesses, a rule the clerk ties to KRS 457.050 effective July 15, 2018.

KRS 382.135 is the source of the in-care-of address and full-consideration requirements, and KRS 382.110 covers the title source. Attorneys catch these routinely. Someone who drafted a deed without one should run through the list.

What transfer tax applies to a Barren County sale?

The seller owes half a dollar for each $500 of value in the deed, with any leftover part of $500 rounded up (KRS 142.050). For a house at the $178,000 median, the deed holds 356 units of $500, and the tax would be $178.00.

The clerk figures the amount and holds the deed until it is paid. No tax applies to a deed that only fixes an earlier deed, ties or frees a debt, follows a foreclosure, or passes between spouses, nor to a parent-child transfer for token consideration. For a gift, the base is market value.

How do delinquent taxes and liens show up in Barren County?

Once sheriff season closes, an unpaid Barren County bill is the clerk's responsibility, since the Legal Records Division collects delinquent real estate taxes. Per the state revenue department, April 15 is the cutoff. The clerk then holds a certificate of delinquency, a lien goes on record, interest of 1 percent monthly begins, and fees for the county attorney and clerk follow.

KRS 134.015 sets December 31 as the due date, a 2 percent discount through November 1 and a 5 percent penalty in January. Because the balance grows monthly, get the clerk's payoff figure close to the closing date.

Does the local economy change how fast Barren County houses sell?

Agriculture is the county's main industry, Glasgow is its manufacturing, medical and retail center, and Cave City lives on visitors to Mammoth Cave. In February 2026 a data-center equipment maker announced a $76 million plant in Glasgow expected to bring 400 manufacturing jobs, the largest job announcement in the county in nearly two decades. Where the jobs will sit is clear, near Glasgow. Farm and lake properties elsewhere in the county are a different kind of sale.

Paperwork differs by parcel type. A farm may involve several tracts and an older plat, and a lodging lot near Cave City may carry easements. Each such document is recorded at the clerk, at prices like those in the table.

How do you search Barren County land records online?

Online land records come through eCCLIX, sold by Software Management, LLC. A monthly account costs $200 to start, $65 monthly and $10 per extra user; a one-day account costs $45 to start and $15 for each 24 hours. Walk-in viewing at the clerk's office costs nothing.

DocAlert is a free email notice, run by the same vendor, that fires when a mortgage or deed is filed under a registered personal or business name. Landlords with several parcels, and heirs who live far away, can use it to spot a forged filing.

Closing agents who prefer not to visit the square can file electronically through CSC, Simplifile or ePN. Each vendor's contact details are posted on the clerk's recording page.

  • Agree on who files the deed, electronically or in person in Glasgow.

The office is inside the Barren County Government Center at 117 North Public Square, Suite 1A, Glasgow, and answers at 270-651-3783.

Yes. CSC, Simplifile and ePN are listed e-recording services, so a title company can file without bringing paper to Glasgow.

The clerk may return it. KRS 382.135 calls for an in-care-of address for that year's bill, and the clerk's rejection list names a missing address.

Yes, DocAlert. Sign up on the clerk's website with a name and an email address, and a message goes out whenever a deed or mortgage is recorded under that name.

The Census Bureau counts 301.9 people per square mile, far more crowded than a typical Bluegrass county.

Steel, refining and activated carbon have been the big employers, and the county's population has slid from about 55,500 in 1980 to an estimated 47,751 in 2025. Boyd County Public Schools, Ashland Independent and Fairview Independent each cover part of the county, and buyers usually ask which one serves your street.

What does the Boyd County Clerk charge to record?

On the clerk's fee schedule dated January 1, 2020, a deed is $50 and a mortgage is $80. Added pages and added parcel references raise the total, so phone 606-739-5116 for the current figure.

How is the transfer tax figured in Boyd County?

The bottom of Boyd's schedule prints the transfer tax as a dollar per thousand dollars of value. The person selling pays it, and the clerk takes payment when the deed is handed over.

The Census Bureau's five-year survey puts a typical owner-occupied Boyd County home at $130,700. A sale there comes to 262 steps of $500, or $131.00 in tax. A $90,000 sale comes to $90.00. With prices this low, the tax is usually a smaller line on the settlement statement than the title charges.

Foreclosure transfers, spousal transfers and token-price deeds within a family can be exempt. If you are unsure about yours, ask the clerk before you sign, because a deed cannot be accepted until the right amount is paid.

What has to be in a deed before the clerk will accept it?

KRS 382.135 spells out what a Kentucky deed must carry: both parties' full names and mailing addresses, the whole price, and an address for the current year's tax bill.

  • For a sale, both sides sign a notarized oath that the price in the deed is what was paid.
  • For a gift, the oath says so and adds an estimated fair cash value.
  • The deed points back to the earlier recorded deed or other source of the seller's title.
  • A deed that fails these tests is refused at the counter.

The grantor's recorded source of title is the item most often missing from do-it-yourself deeds. If your deed came from a family member years ago and was never recorded, tell your closing attorney early, since a gap there can hold up a cash closing.

How do inherited Boyd County homes get recorded?

The executor or administrator swears out an affidavit naming each person who receives property and its value, and files it with the clerk. Boyd's schedule prices that affidavit at $50 and a recorded will at $47.

Estates can sit for months with a house unlisted and utilities running. A buyer who pays cash still needs the record to show who owned the property and who received it. Start with the affidavit, then ask the clerk or an attorney which other papers the county needs.

What does a Boyd County closing look like at the clerk's counter?

A closing attorney or title agent normally carries in the signed deed, the notarized price certificate and a check covering recording and transfer tax. Staff compare the deed to the state's content rules, collect the tax, note the date and amount on the deed and file it.

Plan for a few small costs on top of the deed fee. A release of an existing mortgage lists at $46, and a mortgage payoff means a second recording after closing. For a $130,000 Catlettsburg sale you might see $50 for the deed, $46 for one release and $130.00 in transfer tax, which comes to $226 before page charges. Your closing agent will give you the real totals.

The county courthouse in Catlettsburg dates from 1912, replacing the first one built in 1861. Ashland is the larger city, so many sellers there use the Carter Avenue office and skip the drive to the seat.

Who handles delinquent property taxes in Boyd County?

The Boyd County Clerk's office takes over delinquent taxes from prior years. The county's tax page sends payers to 606-739-5116, option 4.

The Sheriff's Office collects the current year's bill. That split means an old unpaid bill is a clerk question and this year's bill is a sheriff question. A closing agent will check both before a sale funds, and a seller who knows of a delinquent bill should ask the clerk for the payoff amount.

Do older Boyd County deeds sit in other counties' books?

Possibly. Boyd County was formed in 1860 from parts of Greenup, Carter and Lawrence Counties, so a chain of title that reaches back before that date can lead into the records of those older counties. Title examiners follow the chain wherever it goes.

If your family has held the land since the nineteenth century, tell the closing attorney early. A call to the Boyd clerk's main office will show how far back the county's own indexes run.

How tight is the Boyd County housing market?

Owners occupy 70.2% of homes here, typical rent is $849 a month and the typical household earns $61,118. The Census Bureau counts 18.0% of residents in poverty, and the average trip to work takes 22.1 minutes. About 21,818 housing units stood in the county in 2025, and just 12 building permits were issued that year.

With so few new homes going up, sellers here compete mostly with other resale houses. A clean title and a complete deed package are the part you control.

Can I record in the Ashland office instead of Catlettsburg?

Possibly. The county lists Ashland and Cannonsburg offices under the County Clerk, but the page does not say which document types each branch accepts. Call the branch first to confirm it will take your deed.

Where do I pay delinquent Boyd County property taxes from a prior year?

A second counter operates in Wilmore at 210 South Lexington Avenue, weekdays from 9 until 3. The county's listing does not break down which services that branch handles, so ask before you carry a closing package there. Nicholasville is the seat and the largest city, which is why most sellers simply use the courthouse.

A house sale usually leaves three papers for the clerk: the deed to the buyer, the lender's payoff release, and sometimes an affidavit. The buyer's title agent expects all of them indexed before funds are released.

Bring these to the counter:

  • The signed, notarized deed with the sale price stated, because the deed tax is figured from that number.
  • A check for the recording charge and the tax. KRS 64.012 also lists a $5 charge when the clerk notarizes the deed on the spot.
  • The lender's release, if it has not been filed. The posted minimum for a release is $46.

Documents past five pages add $3 per extra page, and a mortgage adds the same amount after page thirty. The state's base figure in KRS 64.012 is $33 for up to five pages, so the clerk's totals clearly stack other charges on top. Treat any posted number as a starting point.

How much deed transfer tax does a Jessamine County seller owe?

The seller pays 50 cents for every $500 of price stated in the deed, with any leftover amount rounded up to a full $500 block. The clerk collects it at the counter, and a deed is not accepted for recording until it is paid.

To see how it works, take the county's Census median home value of $268,100. That is 536 full blocks plus a remainder, so 537 blocks at 50 cents gives $268.50. A $400,000 sale produces $400.00. Only one county collects the tax on a sale, the one holding the land.

  • Parent to child, or grandparent to grandchild, with only token payment.
  • A corrective deed that fixes one already of record.
  • A foreclosure, or a surrender of the home to the lender in lieu of one.
  • A deed that only pledges or frees property as security for a loan.

What happens to the tax bill once the deed is on record?

Unpaid bills pass to the clerk after April 15, and the clerk's website carries a delinquent tax search. State revenue officials say 1 percent monthly interest and commissions begin at that point.   • Land records: eCCLIX covers last-minute title follow-ups, estate settlements and appraisals.

Estate sellers should note that wills and affidavits of descent are recorded at the same counter, at the $47 and $50 starting charges on the fee page. An heir listing an inherited house in Jessamine County should ask the clerk which of those papers the title company will want on record.

The county gained roughly 4,000 residents between the 2020 count of 52,991 and a July 2025 estimate of 57,147, a rise of 7.8 percent. Census figures list 22,061 housing units and 512 building permits in 2025.

Jessamine was split off from Fayette County in December 1798, and the clerk says some of its records date to the 1700s. Today the county belongs to the Lexington-Fayette metro area. To June 30, 1966, for deeds, mortgages and wills. The indexes are free to view at the clerk's office, or by eCCLIX subscription from home.

Which office records deeds for Graves County, KY property?

Take it to the Graves County Clerk in Mayfield. Under KRS 382.110, an instrument has to be recorded where the land lies, or where most of the land lies if it straddles a county line. Filing anywhere else leaves the deed exposed to later buyers who had no notice of it and to creditors.

The Clerk works from 1102 Paris Road, Suite 5, Mayfield, KY 42066, and the county lists its hours as eight to four-thirty. On its county web page, the office is described as the place where deeds, mortgages and encumbrances are kept for public use. Real estate records are handled through the records vault, (270) 247-1697, while title transfers, marriage licenses and vehicle work go through (270) 247-1676.

That office also takes delinquent real estate tax, so one visit can cover an old balance and the new deed.

What are the Graves County Clerk's recording fees?

KRS 64.012 sets the schedule, and the version in force since July 15, 2026 charges $33 to record and index a deed of up to five pages. A mortgage of up to 30 pages is $63. Each page past the limit adds $3, and the Clerk can also collect a $10 reimbursement for permanent storage of the record.

Of every $33 deed fee, the Clerk keeps $27 and $6 is sent to the state's affordable housing trust fund. A seller who needs the Clerk to notarize the deed should budget the $5 on top.

What must a Kentucky deed say before the Clerk will accept it?

KRS 382.135 forbids the Clerk from filing a deed that leaves out required items, so mistakes are stopped at the counter. The deed has to contain:

  • the grantor's and grantee's complete names, and a mailing address for each;
  • the full price or other consideration;
  • a c/o address where that year's property tax bill can be mailed;
  • a notarized certificate from both parties confirming that the stated price is the whole consideration, or, for a gift, saying so and giving an estimate of fair cash value.

KRS 382.110 adds a lineage requirement. The deed must point to the grantor's own source of title, giving the office, book, page and recording date of the earlier deed. If the owner inherited the land, the deed says how and from whom.

Utility easement deeds, cemetery lot deeds, government rights-of-way and deeds that fix errors in an earlier deed are exempt from the price, tax-address and certificate items.

How does an inherited Graves County house reach the buyer?

When an owner dies and the house passes by will or by the intestacy rules, the estate's personal representative files an affidavit with the clerk of every county holding estate land, ahead of closing the estate. It names the people receiving each parcel and the value assigned in handling the estate, or says no value was set.

A Graves County heir selling to a cash buyer should therefore expect two filings at the Clerk's office, the affidavit and the new deed, with the deed charged under the schedule above.

KRS 382.270 adds one more gate. A deed or mortgage does not protect against a buyer for value without notice, or against creditors, until it has been acknowledged or proved as the law directs.

What transfer tax does a Graves County seller owe?

KRS 142.050 puts it on the grantor, meaning the seller, and the Clerk takes payment at the counter before filing the deed. Fifty cents buys each block of $500 in value, and a partial block counts as whole. At the Census median value of $147,800 that comes to 296 units, or $148.

The statute excuses a long list of transfers, among them debt security deeds, divorce transfers between spouses and foreclosure deeds. The Grayson County Clerk page on this site lists the exemptions in more detail.

How are mortgage releases and assignments handled?

A paid-off mortgage is cleared with a release recorded at the Clerk's office. KRS 382.360 permits a margin entry or a separate deed of release, and it spells out that giving the release to the borrower does not satisfy the duty to file it. A seller whose lender never filed can discover the old mortgage still open on the record.

When a lender passes a mortgage to another holder, the new holder files the assignment within 30 days. Missing that deadline does not by itself affect the lien's validity.

A mortgage that keeps a lien in the deed also has to name the source of the borrower's title, and KRS 382.290 lets the Clerk charge the KRS 64.012 fee for each assignment and release noted on the record, paid by the person making the entry.

Ask the records vault before listing whether each earlier mortgage on the parcel shows as released. A paid loan that still shows as open is simpler to correct before a buyer's title search turns it up.

How do I get a certified copy of a recorded Graves County deed?

Ask the records vault. KRS 64.012 prices a certified copy at $5, with half a dollar added for every page past three. KRS 382.110 treats an authentic photocopy that the official custodian certifies as a true, unaltered copy of the original, and a certified copy can be filed in another county's office as if it were the original, provided it meets all the filing rules.

That matters when a parcel crosses a county line or when a lender wants proof of an earlier deed. Title agents sometimes want the last vesting deed in certified form.

  • Bring the grantor name, the approximate year and, if you have them, the deed book and page.
  • Ask whether the copy needs to carry the clerk's certification for out-of-county use.
  • Request a separate copy of any recorded release, so the chain from deed to payoff is complete.

What is Graves County like for a seller?

Graves County sits in far western Kentucky and was formed in 1824. Mayfield is the seat. The county also holds Wingo, a stretch of the Clarks River National Wildlife Refuge, and the Black Patch tobacco history that shaped its farms. A December 10, 2021 tornado caused major damage in Mayfield, including to the courthouse. Census QuickFacts reports:

  • 37,050 residents in 2025 and 14,139 households.
  • Owners occupy 76.1 percent of homes, which have a median value of $147,800.
  • Median gross rent of $775.
  • Retail sales of $808,990,000 in 2022, or $22,168 per person.

A seller who keeps the recorded paperwork in order, from the last vesting deed to the mortgage release, avoids the delays that title problems cause.

Frequently asked questions

Which office files deeds for a house in Graves County?

The Graves County Clerk, 1102 Paris Road, Suite 5, Mayfield. Call the records vault at (270) 247-1697 with questions about real estate filings.

What does recording a deed cost in Graves County?

Thirty-three dollars buys a recording of up to five pages, with $3 for each page beyond that and a $10 storage reimbursement. Transfer tax is charged separately.

Can the Clerk turn my deed away?

Yes. KRS 382.135 bars filing a deed that lacks names, addresses, the consideration statement, a tax-bill address or the sworn certificate, and the deed must also cite its source of title.

Is a mortgage release my lender's job or mine?

The lender or holder signs it, but it only counts once it is filed with the Clerk. Handing a copy to the borrower is not enough, so ask the records vault whether it appears on your parcel.

What do heirs file before selling an inherited Graves County house?

The personal representative lodges an affidavit at the Clerk's office naming each recipient and an estimated value, and the new deed follows. KRS 382.135 calls for it before the estate is closed.

Bourbon County covers about 290 square miles of gently rolling farmland in the Lexington area, with Paris as the seat and Millersburg and North Middletown as the other incorporated towns. It is one of Kentucky's nine original counties, formed in 1785.

The clerk's is a constitutional office whose duties come from the Kentucky Revised Statutes. Besides recording, it prepares property tax bills, runs elections and titles vehicles. Fayette was one of the three original counties created in 1780, and its land records reach back to about 1792, the year Kentucky became a state. They exist in books, on microfilm and as digital images.

For a seller, the clerk is the last stop on a sale. The deed is signed, the transfer tax is paid, and recording puts the buyer's ownership on the public record. Most of the paperwork rides along with the closing agent, but knowing the rules helps when a deed is signed outside a title office.

What formatting rules does the Fayette County Clerk enforce on deeds?

The Kentucky County Clerks Association adopted the Property Records Industry Association standards for real estate documents on January 1, 2020, and Fayette applies them. A document that breaks the rules can be turned away at the desk, so check the layout before the signing appointment.

  • Paper: 20 lb white stock with no watermarks, 8.5 by 11 inches preferred and 8.5 by 14 accepted, printed on one side only.
  • Margins: leave 3 inches blank at the top of page one for the recorder's stamp, and 1 inch elsewhere.

It covers deeds, quitclaim deeds, easements, powers of attorney, land contracts, affidavits of descent or heirship, mortgages, releases, lis pendens notices, judgment and mechanic's liens, and wills. A corrective deed or an affidavit of heirship goes through the same desk.

The levy falls on the grantor and counts every $500 of declared value, rounding a partial block up. Where does Pendleton County record a deed?

Every land record in the county ends up in Falmouth, at the Pendleton County Clerk's office, 233 Main Street, Room 1 (KY 41040). Letters go to PO Box 112, calls to 859-654-3380 and faxes to 859-654-5600.

The clerk's website shows weekday service from half past eight until four, plus Saturday mornings on two weekends a month (the second and the last), closing at noon, holiday weekends excepted. Recording happens where the land is, as KRS 142.050 indicates by pointing to KRS 382.110, so a house near Butler or DeMossville is recorded in Falmouth even if the seller has moved away.

What should a seller know about Pendleton County itself?

About 280 square miles of rolling hills make up Pendleton County, roughly midway between Cincinnati and Lexington, within the Cincinnati metropolitan area. The Ohio River borders it to the northeast. The seat, Falmouth, stands where the Main and South Licking rivers come together, and the other city, Butler, is on the Licking about 10 miles upstream to the north. DeMossville is an unincorporated community.

The county, formed in 1798 from Campbell and Bracken counties, honors Edmund Pendleton, a Virginia jurist. Falmouth started as Forks of Licking around 1776, was chartered in 1793, became the seat in 1799 and built its present courthouse in 1848. The Kentucky Central Railroad brought Butler into being around 1852, and the town was incorporated on February 1, 1868. A Union Army recruiting camp opened in Falmouth in September 1861. Men from the county fought in both armies in the Civil War, and a brief skirmish took place at Falmouth on September 18, 1862. Landmarks include Bethel Cemetery and Church, a frame church five miles north of Falmouth, and the 1811 stone Fryer House, home of the county historical society. Kincaid Lake State Park spreads over 850 acres with camping, golf, swimming and fishing.

How has Pendleton County's population changed?

The population hit a high of 16,702 in 1880, fell to 9,610 in 1950 and stood at 14,877 in 2010. By 2020 it was 14,644, and the Census Bureau estimates 14,800 for mid-2025. In 2020 all residents counted as rural, the median age was 41.6, and 11.7 percent of the 6,263 housing units were vacant. Of the 5,533 households then, 32.4 percent had children under 18 and 24.7 percent were one person living alone. The homeowner vacancy rate was 1.3 percent, against 5.6 percent for rentals.

  • Owner-occupied homes are worth $159,800 at the median, and 74.7 percent of the 5,442 households own.
  • A mortgage holder pays $1,172 monthly, and a renter pays $793.
  • The median household earns $64,669, and 13.7 percent of residents live below the poverty line.
  • Commutes average 36.4 minutes.
  • None of the 6,341 housing units were added by permit in 2025.

What has to appear in a deed before the clerk files it?

KRS 382.135 forbids a clerk to file a deed missing any of these four things.

  • Each party's full name and mailing address.
  • The entire price, written as consideration.
  • A care-of address for the tax bill that covers the transfer year.
  • A sworn, notarized statement from both parties that the price shown is the whole price, or for a gift an estimate of fair cash value.

Deeds limited to utility easements, government rights of way or cemetery lots, and deeds fixing mistakes in an earlier deed, are excused from the last three items.

How is transfer tax figured on a Pendleton County sale?

The grantor pays fifty cents on every $500 of value, counting a partial $500 as whole, before the deed is accepted (KRS 142.050). A $159,800 deed at the county median covers 320 units, so the tax is $160.00. The clerk retains 5 percent as a collection fee, and the county treasurer receives the rest quarterly.

Corrective deeds, deeds that give or lift security for a debt, spouse transfers, foreclosure transfers and parent-to-child transfers for token money escape the tax. A gift is measured by what the house would sell for on the open market.

What about inherited houses or houses with liens?

When a house comes down through a will or intestacy, the personal representative must file an affidavit with the clerk before the estate closes, naming each recipient and what the property is worth (KRS 382.135(4)). The clerk lists $50 for an affidavit of descent and $46 for a will.

Liens go on record at the same counter. Recording a certificate of delinquency costs $46, and so does its release. State revenue guidance says unpaid property tax passes from the sheriff to the county clerk after April 15, with a lien recorded on the parcel. Judgment and mechanics' liens cost $46 in each direction. A parcel search at the clerk's counter before listing can head off surprises.

What should a Pendleton County seller prepare before closing?

  • Find the deed book and page for your own title.
  • See whether a lien, lis pendens or certificate of delinquency is on record.
  • Pick the mailing address for the buyer's first bill.
  • Book a notary for the sworn price statement.
  • Request one total for recording fees and transfer tax.

An heir with an empty Pendleton County house who prefers not to make repairs can request a cash offer, and the buyer's closing agent then takes care of recording.

What do Pendleton County's economic figures suggest?

Business activity is small. Employers numbered 172 in 2023 and provided 1,644 jobs with $78.8 million in payroll, and employment fell 5.1 percent from the year before. Shops sold $60.7 million in 2022, which is $4,128 per resident, and health care and social assistance brought in $13.6 million. A further 831 nonemployer businesses were active in 2024.

Bachelor's degrees belong to 15.4 percent of adults, 17.6 percent of people under 65 report a disability, and 9.2 percent of them lack health insurance. Most residents (90.8 percent) were in the same house a year earlier, 737 are veterans, and 19.9 percent are 65 or older. Broadband reaches 81.1 percent of households, and the typical household has 2.66 people. Per capita income is $31,070, owners with no mortgage pay a median $475 a month, and the county's 277 square miles of land hold about 52.8 people per square mile, denser than Owen County's 32.1.

Weekdays until 4 p.m., opening at 8:30 a.m., and on the second and last Saturday of each month until noon, barring a holiday weekend.

Yes, at $50 per the fee list, or $96 when a revocation is recorded with it.

Where can I get a certified copy of my deed?

At the Pendleton County Clerk in Falmouth, which charges $5 for a certified copy and $2 for a standard one.

What role does the Greenup County Clerk play in a sale?

The Clerk puts the sale on the public record by recording the deed and any mortgage. For a seller, recordings and delinquent bills are the two that matter.

A house in Greenup, Flatwoods, Raceland, Russell, South Shore, Worthington or Wurtland is recorded in this office, because deeds go to the clerk of the county where the land sits. Documents can go through an e-recording vendor or be brought to a counter. Ask the title company or closing attorney who handles the recording and the transfer tax, and keep the recorded copy.

The Clerk also takes the unpaid tax bills that the sheriff passes along after April 15 and runs the sale of those bills. Our Greenup County property tax guide covers that side in detail.

Where are the Clerk's offices and what hours do they keep?

Three offices serve the county, each open Monday to Friday, 9:00 a.m. until 4:30 p.m. Mail for the main office goes to PO Box 686, Greenup, KY 41144. South Shore shuts for lunch between noon and 1:00 p.m.

What transfer tax applies to a Greenup County sale?

The Clerk's FAQ lists the tax as an add-on to the recording fee, so the two appear as separate amounts. Add them for a rough total. On a $134,000 sale, the deed fee plus the tax comes to $184 before extra pages.

DOCALERT is a free service the Clerk's office offers through Software Management, LLC. Signing up takes a name and an email address. After that, any mortgage or deed filed in Greenup County under your personal or business name triggers a message to you.

It suits anyone who owns a house they do not live in: a landlord, an heir holding a parent's home, or an owner of a vacant property. If a deed or mortgage you never signed is recorded, the message gives you a reason to call the Clerk and an attorney.

How does the Clerk handle delinquent property tax?

Every unpaid real property bill reaches the Clerk from the sheriff on April 15, and a lien is recorded against each parcel. Bills still open later are sold. The Clerk's delinquent taxes page links third-party purchaser information, an application and the state's delinquent tax listing.

Under the state process, the sale lands 90 to 135 days after the transfer, the county attorney sends notices, and the bills are advertised 30 to 45 days ahead. After it, the lien belongs to a third-party purchaser and you pay that buyer.

Why does a Louisville home sale go through the Jefferson County Clerk?

The Legal Records Division of the Jefferson County Clerk's office is the official repository for deeds, mortgages, releases and liens on Louisville real estate. Until your deed is taxed, accepted and indexed there, the sale does not show on the public record.

The Deed Room works out of Metro Hall, 527 W. Jefferson St., Room 204, Louisville, KY 40202, and its listed telephone is 502-574-6220. Wills and name changes pass through that same room after the probate court signs off, which helps if you inherited the house. Tax collection after April 15 sits at a different counter, Suite 100a in the same building.

The office runs a free alert service called ClerkAlert. It emails owners whenever a paper is filed under their name or business name, and some sellers keep it switched on after closing as a guard against forged deeds or surprise liens.

What does the Clerk charge to record a deed in Louisville?

A deed costs $50 and a mortgage costs $80. The clerk lists the full price list under KRS 64.012, as amended by Senate Bill 114, and the sample below is copied from that list.

Recording prices posted by the Jefferson County Clerk for common real estate papers
Paper filedPrice

Several add-ons can raise the bill:

  • Instruments sent through the mail pick up a $1 postage charge starting September 1, 2026.
  • Certified copies cost $5 for three pages, then 50 cents a page.
  • Each extra book or reference tied to a document adds $4.
  • The clerk's in-house notary charges $2 per signature.

How does the state transfer tax work on a Jefferson County deed?

The seller owes it. KRS 142.050 taxes the grantor named in the deed at 50 cents for each $500 of declared value, rounding any leftover amount up to the next $500, and the clerk collects before recording.

Run the numbers for a house worth $248,400, the Census figure for a typical owned home here. That value holds 497 units of $500 after rounding up, so the tax is $248.50. Look for that charge on your settlement statement as its own line, apart from the recording fee.

Some transfers pay nothing. The ones sellers meet most often are these:

  • Husband and wife, or ex-spouses in a divorce.
  • A deed that only secures or releases a debt.
  • A corrective deed that confirms one already on record.
  • A foreclosure sale, or a voluntary surrender in lieu of foreclosure.
  • Parent and child, or grandparent and grandchild, when only nominal money changes hands.

The Clerk's checklist asks that a deed claiming exemption name the statute behind it.

What makes the Clerk turn a deed away?

Papers that miss the formatting or content checklist are returned at the counter. The checklist borrows the PRIA national layout standards that the Kentucky County Clerks Association adopted for filings from 2020 onward.

  • White letter-size paper, printed one side, with no staples, binding, embossed seals or highlighter.
  • Ten-point Times New Roman or a close match, black ink, and a three-inch blank band atop page one.
  • A preparation statement signed by whoever prepared the document. A "Drafted by" line does not count.
  • Full addresses for both parties, and a mailing address for future tax bills.
  • A legal description, the deed or will book and page of the seller's title, and a stated fair market value.
  • A notary block showing the notary's ID number and naming grantor and grantee.
  • An original or certified copy with the right fee in a signed check.

If the seller is a corporation, LLC or partnership, the Secretary of State must have the entity on file before the clerk will take its deed. Settle that point a week or two before the closing date.

How are mortgage payoffs recorded in Jefferson County?

Your lender files a release at $46 after the payoff clears. When a deed and a release travel together, the posted price for the pair is $96.

The Clerk's guidance reminds filers that a mortgage is recorded where the land sits, per KRS 382.110, and that it binds third parties from the moment it is acknowledged and recorded under KRS 382.080. The release must cite the book and page of the mortgage it wipes out, and the closing agent usually gets that from the title search.

Request a payoff letter that stays good through the closing date. Afterward, ask the title company when the release went out. A mortgage that stays open on the Jefferson County record can complicate the next owner's loan.

How does unpaid property tax reach the Clerk?

At the close of business on April 15, any current-year bill still open leaves the Sheriff and lands with the Clerk as a certificate of delinquency. By then the Sheriff's schedule has added a 10 percent penalty and a 10 percent add-on fee, and the Clerk's side starts adding interest at 1 percent per month.

The County Attorney's tax page puts the combined extra cost near 40 percent once a certificate exists, and says certificates accrue interest at 12 percent a year. Each summer the Clerk holds a lien sale, and bills that fail to sell stay open for purchase all year. A buyer of a certificate can pile its own charges on top.

If nobody has bought the certificate, pay the Clerk at 527 W. Jefferson St., Room 100. Mailed payments must be certified or cashier's checks or money orders, because the office rejects personal checks and phone payments. A bill placed on a County Attorney payment plan cannot be sold at the sale.

Sellers should order a payoff figure before the listing goes live. Then the buyer's title company can settle it out of the proceeds.

What do sellers need to know about Jefferson County itself?

Kentucky's largest county covers 380.8 square miles of land along the Ohio River, and since the 2003 merger its lines match those of Louisville, the county seat. Jeffersontown, St. Matthews, Middletown and dozens of smaller cities still keep their own governments inside Louisville Metro.

Public schools come from Jefferson County Public Schools and the Anchorage Independent district, which stops at eighth grade. Census QuickFacts reports:

  • 795,222 residents in the 2025 estimate, up 1.6 percent from the April 2020 base.
  • 366,702 housing units counted in 2025.
  • 62.1 percent of households own their home (2020 to 2024).
  • $248,400 as the typical owned-home value.
  • $1,149 as median gross rent.

The PVA's count of 83 taxing jurisdictions includes about 60,000 properties in the smaller home rule cities, many of which send their own bill. Recording works the same across all of them, but a seller in a small city should check for a city tax balance before closing.

Frequently asked questions

Which office takes a deed for a house in Louisville?

The Jefferson County Clerk's Legal Records Division, in the Deed Room at Metro Hall, 527 W. Jefferson St., Room 204. Phone 502-574-6220. The closing agent normally files for the buyer, and the office also takes electronic filings.

What will I pay to put a deed on record?

The posted rate is $50 for a deed and $96 when a release is filed with it. Mailed instruments add $1 for postage from September 1, 2026, and the separate transfer tax runs 50 cents per $500 of value.

Is the transfer tax charged to me or to the buyer?

Charged to you as grantor. KRS 142.050 imposes it on the seller named in the deed. Transfers such as those between spouses or through foreclosure are exempt when the deed cites the exemption.

Why would the Clerk reject my paperwork?

Typical causes are a missing preparation statement, no source of title, no stated market value, no tax-bill mailing address, a weak notary block or the wrong fee. An LLC seller also has to be registered with the Secretary of State first.

I owe back tax on the house. Where do I start?

Ask the Sheriff for any current-year balance before April 15, and the Clerk for older certificates afterward. Get both figures in writing before listing so the title company can pay them at closing. The County Attorney's Tax Division handles payment plans.

State law ties the filing to the land, so a seller in Whitesburg, Jenkins, Fleming-Neon, Blackey, McRoberts or any smaller community uses this one office. Closing agents either walk the paper in or send it through an e-recording vendor the clerk names: Indecomm, Hopdox, CSC, Simplifile or ePN.

What should a Letcher County home seller know about the area?

Letcher County is in the far southeast corner of Kentucky, on the Virginia line. The state formed it in 1842 as its 95th county out of Harlan, Perry and Pike, and named it for the governor of the day. Whitesburg is the seat, called Summit City until 1842, and Jenkins is the largest city. Pine Mountain runs 125 miles across the region and splits the county, Black Mountain on the southeast edge tops out near 3,700 feet, and the North Fork of the Kentucky River runs through Whitesburg. Coal mining shaped the towns, and the county's roughly 338 square miles of land are steep and wooded.

  • Population: 19,952 in the July 2025 estimate, against 21,548 in the 2020 count and 24,519 in 2010.
  • Housing: 10,716 units and 8,463 households, with 74.1 percent owner occupied (2020 to 2024 survey).
  • Middle home value: $67,400, with rent at a median of $669.
  • Median household income: $41,793, with 25.3 percent of residents in poverty and 21.9 percent aged 65 or older.

Most students attend Letcher County Public Schools, while the far eastern end of the county around Jenkins is served by Jenkins Independent Schools. U.S. 119 links Jenkins to Whitesburg and crosses Pine Mountain, and U.S. 23 passes through the eastern part of the county. Roughly 43 percent of residents age 16 and over are in the civilian labor force, and the mean trip to work takes 28.3 minutes.

Floods in July and August 2022 killed three people in the county and left many residents without homes. If a house took water, ask the lender and closing agent how that history affects insurance and underwriting.

What does the Letcher County Clerk need to see on a deed?

The clerk's deeds page lists what a conveyance must carry before staff can file it. Hold a draft up against this list before the signing appointment.

  • Names and mailing addresses for both seller and buyer, and a return mailing address.
  • A legal description and the source of the seller's title.
  • A consideration statement signed by both sides and notarized.
  • A preparation statement.
  • An in-care-of address where the property tax bill for the year of transfer can go (required on deeds signed on or after August 1, 2008).

A notary must witness the seller's signature. Nearly every deed also needs the sworn consideration statement. The clerk lists the exceptions: utility easements, divorce transfers ordered by a court, rights of way for government agencies, cemetery lots, and corrective deeds between the same two parties. Under KRS 382.110 a lender that accepts a deed in lieu of foreclosure must file it inside 45 days.

How is transfer tax calculated on a Letcher County sale?

The seller bears this tax. The rate is $0.50 per $500 slice of the price in the deed, rounded up, and the clerk's FAQ restates it as $1.00 per $1,000. Its worked example prices a deed at $10,000 and gets $10.00 in tax before the filing fee. A deed at Letcher County's median home value of $67,400 spans 135 slices and owes $67.50.

Where a deed is a gift or names a nominal price, the market value stands in for the price. Collection happens once per transaction, in the recording county, and staff will not file a deed with the tax unpaid. KRS 142.050 exempts these transfers:

  • Foreclosures and voluntary surrenders to a lender.
  • Moves between spouses, or ex-spouses under a divorce.
  • Token-price deeds from parent to child or grandparent to grandchild.
  • Deeds that exist only to secure or free up a debt, or to fix an earlier deed.
  • Tax sale deeds and partitions.

On a land contract, the tax comes due when the deed is later delivered, not when the contract is recorded.

The clerk's website vendor, Software Management, runs two kinds of online access. Businesses that research documents for a living subscribe. A Letcher County resident looking up records for personal reasons pays nothing but is capped at five searches a day and can see Letcher County only.

A separate free tool, DOCALERT, sends an email whenever a mortgage or deed is filed under a name you register, personal or business. Signing up takes a name and an email address. Owners of vacant or inherited property that has not been retitled may find it worth the two minutes.

  • Find the deed you received, since its recording details feed the new deed's source of title.
  • Get a payoff figure from the lender and confirm who files the mortgage release.
  • Get the buyer's in-care-of address for the tax bill.
  • Compute the transfer tax from the contract price, or check whether an exemption applies.
  • Ask the closing agent whether the deed will be walked in or e-recorded.

A house with repair needs, unsettled heirs or flood damage can also go to a direct cash buyer. The deed, tax and recording rules do not change with the buyer.

It is 156 Main Street, Suite 102, in Whitesburg, KY 41858, and the number is (606) 633-2432. Weekday hours run 8:30 to 4:00, and the doors stay shut on weekends.

Expect $50 for five pages plus $3 per added page, then the seller's transfer tax. The clerk's deeds page also describes a $4 state legal process tax on conveyances, collected with the filing fee.

Does a Letcher County deed need a notary?

Yes. The seller's signature is acknowledged before a notary, and both parties sign the consideration statement in front of one too. The clerk charges $2.00 to notarize a document at the office.

Is online deed searching free in Letcher County?

For residents researching personal matters, yes, up to five searches a day in Letcher County records. Commercial researchers pay a subscription.

Does a house gift to a child owe transfer tax?

No, when the price is nominal and the deed runs from parent to child or grandparent to grandchild, which KRS 142.050 exempts. A gift deed to anyone else is taxed on open market value.

The buyer may sue to foreclose one year after the certificate is created. Because the property carries a lien until the bill is paid in full, a seller who sees an unpaid year in the file should resolve it before a buyer's title company does.

The same office licenses vehicles, runs elections, issues notary bonds, and processes delinquent real estate taxes. The land records page says recorded instruments reach back to 1786, though the county itself dates from 1860. Disputes about records or fines go elsewhere: the courts answer at 270-639-9160 or 270-639-9300.

The posted schedule took effect January 1, 2020. Each page past the fifth costs $3, and for mortgages the $3 starts after page thirty. A separate $4 state tax on each real property conveyance comes from KRS 142.010; the clerk collects and remits it. Check whether a quoted total includes it.

Minimum amounts posted by the Anderson County Clerk for frequent real estate filings (anderson.countyclerk.us)
FilingMinimum

Mortgage$80

A seller typically pays for a deed and perhaps a release, so the clerk's charges are a small slice of closing costs.

How does the state transfer tax work in Anderson County?

Under KRS 142.050 the seller pays $0.50 for each $500 declared in the deed, and a partial $500 counts as a whole one. The clerk does the math and keeps the deed until payment. Picture a $225,100 sale: 450 whole units plus a remainder make 451 units, so the tax is $225.50.

A gift, or a deed with token consideration, is valued at open-market price. Out of the tax, the clerk retains 5 percent and sends the rest to the county treasurer every quarter. These transfers are exempt:

  • Transfers by foreclosure, or by voluntary surrender under a mortgage.
  • Spouse to spouse, including former spouses dividing property in a divorce.
  • Parent and child, or grandparent and grandchild, for nominal money.
  • Deeds that only secure or free a debt, or correct an earlier deed.
  • Tax-sale conveyances and partitions.

The clerk's records page lists an Exempt Transfer Affidavit, Form 71A245, to claim an exemption.

What else can you do at the Anderson County Clerk's office?

The same counter that records deeds also renews vehicle registrations. The clerk's website asks online renewers for a title number, a plate number and a credit card, and it has a VIN lookup for the prior year's vehicle tax. Voter registration and election results sit in the elections department. A delinquent-tax lookup called DTax lets you check whether a parcel is on the unpaid list, though the site warns the clerk alone fixes the dollar amount owed on any bill when a sale happens.

Common forms are grouped as motor vehicle, legal records, elections and delinquent tax. Sellers mostly need the legal records set, which includes the Exempt Transfer Affidavit, a release of a real estate mortgage, a release of a vendor's lien and an affidavit of conversion to real estate.

How far back do Anderson County land records go?

Deeds and mortgages are indexed in CCLIX to 1966, and wills and marriages to 1797. Document images from January 2004 forward can mostly be pulled up online, while paper and microfilm reach into the 1700s.

Online access runs through eCCLIX, which requires an account from the vendor and charges for use. In the clerk's office anyone can read the same indexes and images without paying. DocAlert is a free email service: register a name, and each deed or mortgage recorded under it triggers a notice. Owners who live elsewhere or hold rentals can use it to catch a fraudulent filing early.

What if the property tax was never paid?

On April 15 the sheriff passes all unpaid bills to the clerk. The Sheriff's Office says payers there owe a 20 percent County Attorney fee and a 10 percent Clerk fee, plus interest of 1 percent monthly, on top of earlier penalties. Summer can bring a sale of the debt to a private buyer.

Under KRS 134.015(5) the lien can follow the land for up to eleven years regardless of owner, and a title agent will find it. Plan for the payoff to come out of the seller's net. Until April 15 the Sheriff's Office takes payment, at (502) 839-4021.

What is a sensible checklist before signing?

  • Find your own deed and record its book and page.
  • Get this year's bill and any old balance from the Sheriff.
  • Ask the clerk about any recorded lien or lis pendens.
  • Write in the buyer's mailing address for the tax bill.
  • Prepare the exemption affidavit if one applies.

Frequently asked questions

Do I still record in Lawrenceburg for a house outside the city?

Yes. Anderson County has one clerk, and KRS 382.110 sends a deed to the clerk of the county holding the land, so a rural parcel goes to the same S Main Street office.

What does the clerk charge at minimum for a deed?

Fifty dollars, with $3 added for each page after the fifth. KRS 142.010 also lays a $4 state tax on conveyances, so ask for the full total first.

Is the seller or the buyer responsible for the transfer tax?

The seller, named as grantor, pays it. KRS 142.050 sets it at half a dollar per $500 of declared value, and the clerk collects it at the counter.

Is browsing old deeds free?

In the office, yes: the clerk says records and indexes are free to view there. Online viewing through eCCLIX costs money.

Is a foreclosure deed taxed?

No. KRS 142.050 exempts foreclosure transfers and voluntary surrenders under a mortgage. The lender then has 45 days from signing to file that deed with the clerk, per KRS 382.110.

Where does a Grayson County, KY deed get recorded?

At the Grayson County Clerk's office, 125 East Market Street, Leitchfield. KRS 382.110 sends every deed to the clerk of the county holding the land, or the larger part of it, and that filing is what lets the deed hold up against later buyers and creditors who never saw it.

The Clerk's website gives two numbers for property work. Recording and delinquent taxes are at (270) 259-5295, and the licensing and transfers desk is at (270) 259-3201. The home page lists weekdays from 8:00 to 4:00, and one Saturday morning a month, the second, from 8:00 to 11:00. A closing set for a particular day is worth a confirming call.

Leitchfield is the county seat and the biggest of the county's three cities, with Caneyville and Clarkson. Big Clifty is a census-designated place. Land in any of them, or out near the lakes, is filed in this one office, and the website's online records section is a place to look up older instruments.

How is the Kentucky transfer tax figured on a Grayson County sale?

Count the sale price in blocks of $500. Each block, including a partial one at the end, carries fifty cents, and the seller is the one taxed. The Clerk does the arithmetic when the deed is presented and holds the deed until payment is made. For a gift or a deed reciting only nominal money, the figure used is what the property would bring on the open market, and any liens count toward the value of a sale.

One transaction is taxed once. The Clerk keeps 5 percent for handling and remits the rest to the county treasurer for the general fund.

Which Grayson County transfers escape the transfer tax?

The statute carves out many cases. A homeowner is most likely to run into the following:

  • a deed given only to secure a debt or to release that security;
  • a correction deed or confirmation of one already of record;
  • a transfer between spouses, or between ex-spouses within a divorce;
  • a foreclosure, or a voluntary surrender to a lender in place of one;
  • a sale for unpaid taxes or assessments, and a partition among co-owners;
  • a nominal-price transfer between parent and child or grandparent and grandchild.

Transfers into a trust escape the tax when the grantor is the lone beneficiary. A clerk who willfully records a taxable deed without collecting can be fined $50 per offense, which explains why the figure in the deed gets checked.

How must a Grayson County deed trace the owner's title?

Every deed has to identify where the grantor's own title came from. If an earlier deed was recorded, the new one cites its office, book, page and recording date. For land received through inheritance or some other unrecorded route, the deed explains how and from whom the grantor took title.

Land assembled from two or more sources gets a deed that names each source and marks which portion came from where. A clerk may not admit a deed missing this trail. Deeds from court commissioners, sheriffs and other court officers acting in their roles are outside the rule.

For a house that has stayed in one family, the earlier deed may be decades old, and the book and page reference is the only link a title examiner follows back. The Clerk's online records section, listed on the office home page, is the first place to look for it.

Before drafting, pull the last vesting deed for the parcel. A wrong book and page cite sends the paper back to whoever prepared it.

What are the filing deadlines for a deed in lieu or a commissioner's deed?

A lender holding a deed in lieu must record it within 45 days of the signing date. A deed handed over by a court-appointed commissioner after a judicial sale must be filed by the grantee inside five business days of receipt. After 30 business days without a filing, a city whose limits include the property can petition Circuit Court for an order compelling the filing, with court costs and attorney fees added.

For an owner in default these dates decide how long the borrower's name stays on the record. Until the lender's deed is filed, the public index still shows the borrower as the owner.

What becomes of unpaid real estate tax in Grayson County?

An unpaid bill leaves the sheriff at closing time on April 15 and goes to the Clerk. The Clerk's recording and delinquent tax number is (270) 259-5295. The Clerk records a lien. Each month, or part of one, adds one percent interest, and both the Clerk and the county attorney charge a commission on top.

The Department of Revenue's sample starts with a $1,000 bill. At transfer the certificate stands at $1,254, and an outside buyer at the sale would pay $1,704.21 under the sample's assumptions, which include a June sale and advertising costs. The sale itself can be scheduled from day 90 to day 135 after transfer. Anyone selling here should ask the Clerk for an exact payoff before the closing date.

What is Grayson County like for a seller?

Grayson County was cut from Hardin and Ohio counties in 1810 and has 497 square miles of land. It lies in the Western Coal Field region, and two Army Corps of Engineers reservoirs, Rough River Lake on the north line and Nolin River Lake on the southeast, give businesses a reason to use the name Twin Lakes. Courthouses burned in 1864, 1896 and 1936. The Western Kentucky Parkway, US 62 and the Paducah & Louisville Railroad cross the county, and it has its own airport. Events fill the calendar too: the Twin Lakes National Fiddlers Contest in July, the county fair around Labor Day, and Clarkson's Honeyfest in September.

  • 27,406 residents in 2025, up 3.7 percent from the 2020 base.
  • 13,496 housing units, and 74.6 percent owner-occupied.
  • A median home value of $164,600 and a median gross rent of $658.
  • Median household income of $50,757, with 22.4 percent of residents below the poverty line.
  • 36 building permits in 2025.
  • 20.2 percent of residents are 65 or older, and the mean trip to work takes 27.9 minutes.
  • In the 2020 census, 21.4 percent of the county's 13,275 housing units were vacant.

With only 36 permits, newly built houses are a small part of what sells. Sellers of older houses with deferred work sometimes choose a buyer who pays cash and takes the property as it is.

Frequently asked questions

What is the address of the Grayson County Clerk?

125 East Market Street, Leitchfield, KY 42754. For recording and delinquent tax questions call (270) 259-5295; weekday hours are posted as 8:00 to 4:00.

Who owes the transfer tax on a Grayson County house sale?

The seller. Fifty cents is charged per $500 of value, so a $164,600 price produces $165 of tax, collected by the Clerk before the deed is recorded.

Does a deed in lieu of foreclosure carry the transfer tax?

No, that transfer is excused by KRS 142.050. The lender must still record the deed within 45 days of signing it.

What happens if my deed does not say where I got title?

The Clerk cannot accept it. The deed must cite the earlier recorded deed by book and page, or explain how title arrived by inheritance or other unrecorded means.

Do old property taxes get paid when a Grayson County house sells?

Yes, normally at closing, since the lien stays on the parcel. Get a payoff quote from the Clerk's delinquent tax line first.
